Contributor Guidelines

ContributorGuidelines.Rmd

CONTRIBUTING.md is a stub that links here.

Branches

  • main — protected. Only merged via pull request; all required checks must be green.
  • {issue#}_short-slug — one feature/fix branch per GitHub issue, cut from main. The issue number prefix ties the branch to the tracker and to the changelog entry.
  • dev branch usage is encouraged but not required before deploying complex changes so that they can be easier reviewed.

Development process

  1. Open a GitHub issue describing the change. Pick the appropriate template from .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/.

  2. Cut a branch named {issue#}_short-slug from main. j block first, then the R code that makes it pass. Every exported function and every non-trivial internal helper gets a direct unit test.

  3. Regenerate documentation and format code before pushing:

    devtools::document()
styler::style_pkg()

  4. Add a bullet to NEWS.md under the current development header.

  5. Open a pull request against main.

Issue-linked tests (qcthat)

Every issue must be covered by qcthat:

  • Link the test that proves the issue’s requirement by putting the issue number in the test_that() title, e.g. test_that("Transform_Range results must match source data (#32)", ...). qcthat ignores issue numbers in comments.
  • Issues that need no test evidence (documentation, CI, refactoring) get the qcthat-nocov label. Obsolete issues are closed as “not planned”.
  • Document the test in the issue in this order: sample data, preparation functions, compared processing paths, output alignment, expected result.
  • Tests for edge cases and errors do not need an issue.
